10.1002_advs.76739: Hydrogen, as a clean and sustainable energy carrier, is currently predominantly produced by electrocatalytic water splitting, which relies on traditional precious-metal-based catalysts. The use of non-precious-metal-based catalysts to promote water splitting driven by renewable energy is gradually gaining favor. Recently, ferroelectric (FE) materials have attracted extensive attention in various catalytic reactions owing to their spontaneous polarization. As a model system with relatively simple reaction pathways, the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) facilitates a deeper understanding of the role of polarization in catalytic mechanisms. This perspective highlights recent advances and conceptual developments in FE catalysts for the HER. First, we introduce the fundamental mechanisms of the HER and ferroelectricity. Second, based on structural design, FE catalysts are classified into single-phase FE catalysts, single-atom modified FE catalysts, FE heterostructure catalysts, and other engineered FE catalysts, and examples of research on each class of FE catalyst for the HER are discussed. Finally, prospects for the future development of FE catalysts for the HER are discussed from the perspectives of intrinsic FE metals, unconventional FE systems, and the coupling of spin with other physical properties. We hope this perspective will provide new insights and research references for exploring FE catalysts for the HER.
10.1002_aenm.71711: As a promising cathode material for large‐scale sodium‐ion energy storage, Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 (NFPP) still suffers from sluggish Na + kinetics and insufficient electronic conductivity. Herein, we propose a bulk‐to‐interface coupling framework in which substitution‐induced electronic regulation propagates from the crystal lattice to the cathode surface, thereby reorganizing the adjacent electrolyte environment. This strategy is implemented by introducing Ni 2 + with high crystal‐field stabilization energy into NFPP. Ni 2+ substitution modulates the local electronic structure, strengthens Fe─O d‐p hybridization, and promotes medium‐range structural ordering. The resulting surface charge redistribution reshapes the interfacial electrostatic potential, suppresses solvent polarization and Na‐ClO 4 association, and facilitates interfacial Na + exchange. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers 118 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and retains 74% of its capacity after 10 000 cycles at 20 C. A pouch cell with a cathode areal capacity of 0.5 mAh cm −2 further demonstrates its feasibility in a full‐cell configuration. This work extends substitution chemistry beyond bulk transport optimization toward the deliberate regulation of electrode‐electrolyte interactions.
10.1021_acs.chemmater.5c01706: Two-dimensional (2D) MXenes have recently attracted substantial attention as promising materials for hydrogen evolution reactions (HER) due to their electrocatalytically active basal plane and tunable electronic properties. In this study, we present a detailed synthesis protocol, preparation, and systematic evaluation of M 4 C 3 T x MXenes for HER activity. We use M 4 C 3 T x MXenes of group five transition metals, namely, V 4 C 3 T x, Nb 4 C 3 T x, and Ta 4 C 3 T x, as our model material system. We provide a detailed description of the synthesis of the MXenes’ precursor phases and their selective etching with hydrofluoric acid, followed by tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAOH)-assisted delamination to obtain single- to few-layered nanosheets. To prepare MXenes for HER testing, we present a universal ion-exchange process to replace the organic cations (tetramethylammonium) with lithium (Li + ) ions, effectively modifying the surface chemistry and interlayer spacing. Finally, we present details of the electrocatalytic HER evaluation study of the Li + -intercalated MXenes in 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 acidic conditions. Our study provides a systematic basis for understanding the preparation–composition–performance relationships in M 4 C 3 T x MXenes and conducting a comprehensive analysis of their HER performance, essential for MXene applications in energy conversion.
10.1021_acs.nanolett.5c06489: The electrosynthesis of cyclohexanone oxime (CHO) from NO is significant but suffers from low Faradaic efficiency (FE) due to the severe competitive NO*–NO* coupling at high NO concentrations. Here, a facet-regulation strategy is proposed to accelerate the NO hydrogenation process and inhibit NO*–NO* coupling. As a result, the Ag nanocubes with {100} surfaces exhibit an 86.5% FE, a 4.45 mmol h –1 cm –2 yield rate, and a 358 mA cm –2 CHO partial current density, outperforming Ag nanohexahedrons with exposed {111} surfaces. Experimental and theoretical research has shown that stronger NO and H 2 O adsorption and lower thermodynamic and kinetic barriers of hydrogenation of NO* to NHO* over the {100} surface promote hydrogenation of NO* to NHO*, the key step that determines the CHO or NO*–NO* coupling products. Thus, NO*–NO* coupling is restrained, and a high CHO FE is achieved on Ag with a {100} surface.
10.1021_acsenergylett.6c00156: We report a two-step thermal evaporation-close space sublimation deposition method for tunable bandgap lead halide perovskites with single junction solar cell efficiencies exceeding 20%. These absorbers are integrated into perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells with stabilized efficiencies of >29%.
10.1021_acsnano.6c15315: Nanoplastics are emerging stressors that perturb host physiology across the gut–immune–brain continuum, yet scalable interventions remain limited. Here, we engineer ZG@EcN@HA, a biohybrid living system created by vacuum-assisted intracellular loading of zinc gluconate into Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) followed by an outer hyaluronic acid (HA) shell. This architecture preserves probiotic culturability under gastric challenge and supports sustained zinc availability in intestinal conditions. In zebrafish chronically exposed to polystyrene nanoplastics, we observe reproducible neurobehavioral impairment coupled with inflammatory activation, redox imbalance, barrier stress, neurotransmitter dysregulation, and multiorgan histopathology. ZG@EcN@HA yields the most coherent rescue compared with single-component controls, restoring behavioral outputs and realigning immune–redox–neurochemical readouts. ASV-based profiling shows recovery of microbial diversity and a shift toward a control-like community structure, including reduced dominance of inflammation-linked taxa. Intestinal transcriptomics and integrative correlation analyses further support normalization of barrier/metabolic programs and attenuation of innate inflammatory signaling. Together, the data identify a materials-enabled strategy for microbiota–gut–brain protection against chronic nanoplastic stress.

10.1039_d5ta09838f: A 2D Bi 2 S 3 decorated 1D SnO 2 , n–n type heterostructure integrated with PEDOT:PSS exhibits photo-assisted supercapacitor and electrochromic behaviour, enabling efficient solar energy conversion, storage, and multifunctional device applications.
